ex.ja: その瞬間、私は現実感を失った。

ex.en: Mr. and Mrs. Smith are a good match.
ex.ja: スミス夫妻は似合いの夫婦だ。

ex.en: Mr Smith is in charge of the class.
ex.ja: スミス先生はそのクラスの担任だ。

note.ja: 古英語 smith（金属を打つ職人）から。blacksmith（鍛冶屋）、goldsmith。姓 Smith の由来。

en: A round or irregular patch on the surface of a thing having a different color, texture etc. and generally round in shape.
A stain or disfiguring mark.
To see, find; to pick out, notice, locate, distinguish or identify.
To stain; to leave a spot (on).
Available on the spot; for immediate payment or delivery.
Exact; precise.

spot.ety:
From Middle English spot, spotte, partially from Middle Dutch spotte (“spot, speck”), and partially merging with Middle English splot, from Old English splott (“spot, plot of land”), from Proto-West Germanic *splott, from Proto-Germanic *spluttaz (“segment”), from Proto-Indo-European *splt-no- (“an off-split, segment”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pel- (“to split”).
Cognate with North Frisian spot (“speck, piece of ground”), Low German spot (“speck”), Old Norse spotti (“small piece”). See also splot, splotch.

ex.en: The goods will be sold on the spot.
ex.ja: その商品は即売されるだろう。

ex.en: The incident left a spot on his reputation.
ex.ja: その事件は彼の名声に汚点を残した。

ex.en: There were ten police officers on the spot.
ex.ja: その現場では１０人の警官がいた。

note.ja: 核のイメージは「小さな点・しみ」。点、しみ、場所（a nice spot）、見つける（点のように目につく）。

en: Traditionally the fourth of the four seasons, typically regarded as spanning either the period between the winter solstice to the spring …
The period of decay, old age, death, or the like.
To spend the winter (in a particular place).
To store something (for instance animals) somewhere over winter to protect it from cold.

winter.ety: From Middle English winter, from Old English winter, from Proto-West Germanic *wintru, from Proto-Germanic *wintruz (“winter”). Cognate with West Frisian winter (“winter”), Dutch winter (“winter”), German Winter (“winter”), Danish, Norwegian Bokmål, Norwegian Nynorsk, and Swedish vinter (“winter”), Faroese and Icelandic vetur (“winter”).

ex.en: There was a lot of snow last winter.
ex.ja: 去年の冬は雪が多かった。

ex.en: Winter sports are very popular in our country.
ex.ja: 我々の国ではウインタースポーツが盛んだ。

ex.en: Some people like summer, and others like winter.
ex.ja: 夏の好きな人もいれば、冬の好きな人もいる。

note.ja: wet、water と同じ祖先とされる「湿った季節」。→「冬」。

en: An opinion offered to guide behavior in an effort to be helpful.
In language about financial transactions executed by formal documents, an advisory document.

ex.en: You had better ask the doctor for advice.
ex.ja: 君は医者に忠告を求めたほうがよい。

ex.en: Let me give you a bit of advice.
ex.ja: 少し忠告したい事がある。

ex.en: You did well not to follow his advice.
ex.ja: 君が彼の忠告に従わなかったのは賢明だった。

note.ja: ad（〜へ）+ vice（見る）。ラテン語 visum から。見方を示すこと →「助言・忠告」。動詞は advise（発音も違う）。

en: An understanding between entities to follow a specific course of conduct.
A state whereby several parties share a view or opinion; the state of not contradicting one another.

ex.ja: 我々はついに合意に達した。

ex.en: Are you in agreement with the new law?
ex.ja: あなたはその新しい法律に賛成ですか。

ex.en: Thank you for the draft of the Agreement.
ex.ja: 契約書のドラフトをありがとうございました。

note.ja: agree（同意する）+ ment。同意したこと →「合意・協定」。

en: A judgment, sentence, or final decision. Specifically: The decision of arbitrators in a case submitted.
The paper containing the decision of arbitrators; that which is warded.
To determine; to make or grant an award.
To give (an award).

ex.en: His new movie earned him an Academy Award.
ex.ja: 新作の映画で彼はアカデミー賞を得た。

ex.en: They awarded her first prize at the flower show.
ex.ja: 花の展示会で、彼らは彼女に１等賞を与えた。

ex.en: The boy was awarded a prize for good conduct.
ex.ja: その少年は善行に対して賞を与えられた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 eswarder（よく見て決める）から。ex + warder（見張る）。「審査して与える」→「賞」。guard、reward と同系。

en: A substantial, often approximately cuboid, piece of any substance.
A chopping block: a cuboid base for cutting or beheading.
To fill or obstruct (something) so that it is not possible to pass.
To prevent (something or someone) from passing.

block.ety: From Middle English blok (“log, stump, solid piece”), from Old French bloc (“log, block”), from Middle Dutch blok (“treetrunk”), from Old Dutch *blok (“log”), from Proto-West Germanic *blokk, from Proto-Germanic *blukką (“beam, log”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰelǵ- (“thick plank, beam, pile, prop”). Cognate with Old Frisian blok, Old Saxon blok, Old High German bloh, bloc (“block”), Old English bolca (“gangway of a ship, plank”), Old Norse bǫlkr (“divider, partition”). More at balk. See also bloc, bulk.

ex.en: She lives a few blocks away from here.
ex.ja: 彼女はここから数区画離れた所に住んでいる。

ex.en: Have you met the new family on the block?
ex.ja: 近所に引っ越してきた家族にはもう会った？

ex.en: Go two blocks along this street and turn left.
ex.ja: この通りを２ブロック行って、左に曲がりなさい。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 blok（木の塊）から。「塊」→ 四角い「街区」→ 行く手を「ふさぐ」。

en: An antagonization or instigation intended to convince a person to perform an action they otherwise would not.
A bid to overcome something.
To invite (someone) to take part in a competition.
To dare (someone).

challenge.ety:
From Middle English chalenge, variant with palatalization of Middle English kalange (“an accusation, claim”), from Old French chalenge, chalonge, palatalized Central French variants of Old Northern French calenge, calonge (see Continental Norman calengier), from Latin calumnia (“a false accusation, calumny”).
Cognate with Old English hōl (“calumny”). Doublet of calumny.

ex.en: Whatever the outcome, you must meet the challenge.
ex.ja: どんな結果になろうとも挑戦は受けなければならない。

ex.en: I don't get enough challenge in this job.
ex.ja: 私はこの仕事にやりがいを感じない。

ex.en: I took a chance and accepted his challenge.
ex.ja: 私は一か八か彼の挑戦を受けてみた。

note.ja: ラテン語 calumnia（中傷）から古フランス語を経た語。「非難する」→「異議を唱える」→「挑む」。

en: A spoken or written remark.
The act of commenting.
To remark.
To make remarks or notes; to express a view regarding.

comment.ety: From Middle English coment, comment, from Old French coment (“commentary”), from Late Latin commentum (“comment, interpretation”), from Classical Latin commentum (“invention, fabrication”).

ex.en: Whoever made that last comment, please leave now.
ex.ja: その最後のコメントをした人は、出ていっていいですよ。

ex.en: Your comments were always very helpful to me.
ex.ja: あなたの批評はいつも私には有益でした。

ex.en: I am not entitled to comment on this.
ex.ja: 私はこのことにコメントする資格はない。

note.ja: ラテン語 commentum（考え出したもの）から。com + mens（心）。「心に浮かんだこと」→「意見・論評」。mental と同じ。

en: The act of equipping, or the state of being equipped, as for a voyage or expedition.
Any items used in equipping something or someone, for example things needed for an expedition or voyage.

equipment.ety: From equip + -ment, or from French équipement.

ex.en: This hospital has a lot of new equipment.
ex.ja: この病院には新しい設備がいろいろ備わっている。

ex.en: This corporation is well known for its communication equipment.
ex.ja: この会社は通信部門でよく知られている。

ex.en: We had a little trouble with the equipment yesterday.
ex.ja: 昨日、私たちはその機材でちょっとしたトラブルがあった。

note.ja: equip（装備する）+ -ment。古フランス語 équiper（船の準備をする）。「装備」。

For some tail; for all terms beyond some term; with only finitely many exceptions.

ex.ja: ゆくゆくは自分の会社を立ち上げようと思っています。

en: Dedicated to a religious purpose or a god.
Revered in a religion.

holy.ety:
From Middle English ali, aly, hale, halege, hali, halȝe, hayly, holi, holia, holie, holiȝ, holy, hooly, oli, oly, wholy, woly, from Old English hāleġ, hāliġ (“holy, sacred; healthy, sound”), from Proto-West Germanic *hailag, from Proto-Germanic *hailagaz (“holy, sacred”), from Proto-Germanic *hailaz (“healthy; whole”), from Proto-Indo-European *kéh₂ilos (“intact, whole; complete; hale, healthy, sound”), equivalent to whole + -y and a doublet of later wholly.

ex.en: The Holy Roman Empire came to an end in the year 1806.
ex.ja: 神聖ローマ帝国は１８０６年に終わりを告げた。

ex.en: This is holy ground.
ex.ja: ここは聖地だ。

ex.en: She always carries the Holy Bible about.
ex.ja: 彼女はいつも聖書を持ち歩いている。

note.ja: 古英語 hālig から。whole（完全な）、health と同じ語根。「完全な」→「神聖な」。holiday は holy day。

en: A historically constituted, stable community of people, formed based on a common economic life, ethnicity, language, religion, and/or ter…
A community united by some trait (especially an interest) but not historically constituted.

From Middle English nacioun, nacion, from Old French nacion, from Latin nātiōnem, accusative of nātiō (“nation”). Displaced Old English þēod and Old English cynewīse.

ex.en: The Queen made an address to the nation.
ex.ja: 女王は国民に向けて演説をした。

ex.en: There are more than 150 nations in the world.
ex.ja: 世界には１５０以上の国がある。

ex.en: The entire nation was glad at the news.
ex.ja: 全国民がそのニュースを聞いて喜んだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 natio（生まれ）から。nat（生まれる）。同じ生まれの人々 →「国民・国家」。native（生まれつきの）、nature（自然）も仲間。

en: Differently, in another way.
In different circumstances; or else.
Other than supposed; different.

otherwise.ety: From Middle English otherwise, othre wise, from Old English on ōþre wīsan (literally “in (on) other/different manner”); equivalent to other + -wise. Compare West Frisian yn oarwei (“otherwise”), Icelandic öðruvísi (“different”).

ex.en: Go at once, otherwise you will be late.
ex.ja: すぐ行きなさい、そうでないと遅れるよ。

ex.en: Hold on tight, otherwise you will fall off.
ex.ja: しっかり捕まえていろ、そうしないと落ちるぞ。

ex.en: Now I am a teacher, I think otherwise.
ex.ja: 先生になった今はそう考えない。

note.ja: other（ほかの）+ wise（方法）。「ほかの方法では」→「さもなければ・それ以外の点では」。

en: First or earliest in a group or series.
Main; principal; chief; placed ahead of others.
A primary election; a preliminary election to select a political candidate of a political party, or the first round of a two-round election.
The first year of grade school.
To challenge (an incumbent sitting politician) for their political party's nomination to run for re-election, through running a challenge…
To take part in a primary election.

primary.ety: Borrowed from Latin prīmārius (“of the first (rank); chief, principal; excellent”), from prīmus (first; whence the English adjective prime) + -ārius (whence the English suffix -ary); compare the French primaire, primer, and premier. Doublet of premier.

ex.en: That primary school has a strong soccer team.
ex.ja: あの小学校はサッカーが強い。

ex.en: Learning to read well is of primary importance.
ex.ja: 読み方をしっかり習うことは最も根本的なことである。

ex.en: The disease is still in the primary stage.
ex.ja: 病気はまだ初期の段階です。

note.ja: ラテン語 primus（第一の）から。prim（第一）+ ary。第一の →「主要な・初等の」。prime（最も重要な）、prince（第一の人→王子）も同じ。

en: The end for which something is done, is made or exists.
Function, role.
To have or set as one's purpose or aim; resolve to accomplish; intend; plan.
To have (an) intention, purpose, or design; to intend; to mean.

purpose.ety: From Middle English purpos, from Old French purposer (“to propose”) (with conjugation altered based on poser), from Latin prō- (“forth”) + pōnere (“place, put”), hence Latin prōpōnō, prōpōnere. By surface analysis, pur- + pose (“halt, pause, put, place”).

ex.en: You made the mistake on purpose, didn't you?
ex.ja: 君は、故意に間違いを犯したんだね。

ex.en: This car is built to serve such purposes.
ex.ja: この車はそんな目的にかなうように作られている。

ex.en: What is the main purpose of this plan?
ex.ja: この計画の主な目的はなんですか。

note.ja: 古フランス語 porposer（意図する）から。pro（前に）+ poser（置く）。「目の前に置いたもの」→「目的」。propose と同じ。

zh: 有責任感的 /有责任感的

en: Having the duty of taking care of something; answerable for an act performed or for its consequences; accountable; amenable, especially l…
Being a primary cause of a situation or action and thus able to be blamed or credited for it.
An actor taking on the lesser roles in repertory theatre.

responsible.ety: From Middle French responsable, from Old French responsable, responsible, formed from the root of Latin responsus, from respondeō, respondēre. The spelling of the English word is taken from the Old French variant responsible. By surface analysis, response + -ible.

ex.en: You are responsible for what you have done.
ex.ja: 君は自分のしたことに対して責任がある。

ex.en: If the machine is damaged, you are responsible.
ex.ja: もしもその機械が壊れたら、君が悪いんだよ。

ex.en: I'm responsible for what my son has done.
ex.ja: 私は息子のしたことに責任がある。

note.ja: re（返して）+ spons（約束する）+ ible（できる）。応答（約束を返すこと）ができる →「責任のある」。

en: An establishment that sells goods or services to the public; originally only a physical location, but now a virtual establishment as well.
A place where things are manufactured or crafted; a workshop.
To visit stores or shops to browse or explore merchandise, especially with the intention of buying such merchandise.
To browse or purchase products from (a catalog, an internet website, etc.), mostly from home.

Cognate with Dutch schop (“shed”), German Schuppen (“shed”), German Schober (“barn”), French échoppe (“booth, shop”) (< Germanic). The verb is denominal. ex.en: The flower shop is just across the street.
ex.ja: 花屋はちょうど通りの向こう側だ。

ex.en: Is there a photo shop in the hotel?
ex.ja: ホテルの中に写真屋はありますか。

ex.en: Is there a flower shop in the hotel?
ex.ja: ホテルの中に花屋はありますか。

note.ja: 古英語 sceoppa（小屋）から。「小屋」→「店」→「買い物をする」。

[with with] Afflicted by (a specific condition, usually medical).
Vomit.
(especially in the phrases on the sick and on long-term sick) Any of various current or former benefits or allowances paid by the Governm…
To vomit.
To fall sick; to sicken.

ex.en: You should take care of your sick mother.
ex.ja: 君は病気のお母さんの面倒をもっと見るべきだ。

ex.ja: 君のお母さんの病気をきづかってやって来ました。

ex.en: Take this medicine in case you get sick.
ex.ja: 具合が悪くなったらこの薬を飲みなさい。

note.ja: 古英語 sēoc から。「病気の」→「吐き気がする」→「うんざりした」→（俗語）「すごい」。

en: A person who teaches, especially one employed in a school; preceptor.
The index finger; the forefinger.

teacher.ety: From Middle English techere, equivalent to teach + -er. More at teach.

ex.en: The teacher gave way to the students' demand.
ex.ja: 教師は学生達の要求に屈した。

ex.en: The school is crying out for good teachers.
ex.ja: 学校では良い教師を切に必要としている。

ex.en: I would like to be an English teacher.
ex.ja: 英語の教師になりたいのです。

note.ja: teach（教える）+ -er。teach は古英語 tǣcan（示す）、token と同系。

en: A description of an event or system that is considered to be accurate.
A coherent statement or set of ideas that explains observed facts or phenomena and correctly predicts new facts or phenomena not previous…

To stay out of the way of (something harmful).

avoid.ety: From Middle English avoiden, from Anglo-Norman avoider, Old French esvuidier (“to empty out”), from es- + vuidier, from Vulgar Latin *vocitāre < Vulgar Latin *vocitum, ultimately related to Latin vacuus. Displaced native Old English forbūgan (literally “to bend away from”).

ex.ja: 私は彼女の目を見るのを避けようとした。

ex.ja: 宗教と政治について論じ合うことは避けたほうがよい。

ex.ja: 戦争は何としても避けなければならない。

The viewpoint in a three-dimensional game or simulation.

ex.ja: これは私が無くしたカメラだ。

ex.ja: これは私がきのう買ったカメラです。

en: A single-room dwelling for a hermit.
A small monastery or nunnery dependent on a larger religious establishment.
To place or enclose in a cell.

cell.ety: From Middle English celle, selle, from Old English cell (attested in inflected forms), from Latin cella (“chamber, small room, compartment”), later reinforced by Old French cel, sele, Old French cele. Ultimately from Proto-Italic *kelnā, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱelneh₂, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to cover”). Doublet of cella and hall. ex.ja: 明日、携帯買うんだよ。

ex.en: Do you have a cell phone with you?
ex.ja: 今携帯持ってる？

ex.en: Please set your cell phones to silent mode.
ex.ja: 携帯をマナーモードに設定してください。

note.ja: ラテン語 cella（小部屋）から。修道院の「小部屋」→ 生物の「細胞」→ 電池、「携帯電話」（cellphone）。cellar と同じ。

en: The edge of the land where it meets an ocean, sea, gulf, bay, or large lake.
To glide along without adding energy; to allow a vehicle to continue moving forward after disengaging the engine or ceasing to apply moti…
To sail along a coast.

ex.ja: 彼は1499年に南アメリカの海岸を訪れた。

en: A substance used to treat an illness, relieve a symptom, or modify a chemical process in the body for a specific purpose.
A psychoactive substance, especially one which is illegal and addictive, ingested for recreational use, such as cocaine.
To administer intoxicating drugs to, generally without the recipient's knowledge or consent.
To add intoxicating drugs to with the intention of drugging someone.

drug.ety: From Middle English drogge (“medicine”), from Middle French drogue, drocque (“tincture, pharmaceutical product”) (c. 1462), from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German droge, as in droge vate (“dry vats, dry barrels”), mistaking droge for the contents, which were usually dried herbs, plants or wares. ex.en: This dog is trained to smell out drugs.
ex.ja: この犬は麻薬を嗅ぎ出すよう訓練されている。

ex.en: I believe more in diet than in drugs.
ex.ja: 薬より食餌療法の方が効くと信じています。

ex.en: We haven't tried the drug out on humans yet.
ex.ja: その薬は人間に対してはまだ実験していない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 drogue から。中世オランダ語 droge（乾いた）とされ、乾燥させた薬草を指した。

en: The study of money, currency and trade, and the efficient use of resources.
Frugal use of resources.
Cheap to run; using minimal resources; representing good value for money; economical.
In or via the part of a commercial passenger airplane reserved for those paying the lower standard fares.

economy.ety: From Middle English yconomye, yconomy, borrowed via Old French yconomie or Medieval Latin from Latin oeconomia, from Ancient Greek οἰκονομία (oikonomía, “management of a household, administration”), from οἶκος (oîkos, “house”) + νέμω (némō, “distribute, allocate”). ex.ja: アメリカ経済は順調ですよ。

ex.ja: 日本の経済についてどう思いますか。

ex.ja: その町は成長して経済の中心となった。

The natural world or ecosystem.

A payment made in accordance with an insurance policy or a public assistance scheme.
To be or to provide a benefit to.
To receive a benefit (from); to be a beneficiary.

ex.ja: 君は自分のためになるような書物を読むべきだ。

In the public eye.

To be placed or situated.

The terrain and conditions surrounding the disc before it is thrown.

en: Either of a pair of people or things that belong together.
Someone who is associated with another in a common activity or interest.
To join as a partner.
To work or perform as a partner.

ex.ja: あなたと私は仕事のよきパートナーです。

To form by the accumulation of materials or constituent parts; to build up; to erect.
A shot in which the delivered stone bumps another stone forward.
A bet that increases the previous bet.

ex.ja: ロス育ちかと思いました。

note.ja: 古北欧語 reisa から。rise（上がる）の他動詞形。「上げる・育てる・（問題を）提起する」。

Appearing sorrowful.

ex.ja: なぜ彼女はあんなに悲しそうなのだろう。

ex.en: The old castle is in a sad state.
ex.ja: その古城は荒れ果てている。

ex.en: The song is at once sad and beautiful.
ex.ja: その歌は悲しくまた美しい。

note.ja: 古英語 sæd（満ち足りた）から。「飽きた」→「重苦しい」→「悲しい」。satisfy と同じ祖先。

en: A homogeneous mixture, which may be liquid, gas or solid, formed by dissolving one or more substances.
An act, plan or other means, used or proposed, to solve a problem.
To treat with a solution.

ex.ja: すみません。この電車はワシントン広場へいきますか。

The underlying shape of a solid.
To give structure to; to arrange.

To cause (someone) to become breathless, as by a blow to the abdomen, or by physical exertion, running, etc.

ex.en: This wind is a sign of a storm.
ex.ja: この風は嵐の前兆だ。

Disturb the peace of mind of; afflict with mental agitation or distress; to exercise.
A strong feeling of anxiety.
An instance or cause of such a feeling.

ex.ja: 初めのうちは私は自分の誤りが気になりました。

To mark (especially cattle) with a brand as proof of ownership.

ex.ja: 「君の車はどこの製品ですか」「フォード社のです」

ex.ja: 私たちはワインは最優良品のみ使っている。

ex.ja: とても気分がリフレッシュされる。

Cognate with Saterland Frisian spreede (“to spread”), West Frisian spriede (“to spread”), North Frisian spriedjen (“to spread”), Dutch spreiden (“to spread”), Low German spreden (“to spread”), German spreiten (“to spread, spread out”), Danish sprede (“to spread”), Norwegian spre, spreie (“to spread, disseminate”), Swedish sprida (“to spread”), Latin spernō, spargō, Ancient Greek σπείρω (speírō), Persian سپردن

ex.en: We should check the spread of the disease.
ex.ja: 我々は病気の伝染をくいとめなければならない。

ex.en: The fire spread out in a fan-shape.
ex.ja: 火は末広がりに大きくなった。

ex.en: Mary spread the big map on the table.
ex.ja: メアリーは机の上に大きな地図を広げた。

note.ja: 古英語 sprǣdan から。「広げる・広がる」→ パンに塗る「スプレッド」。

en: To provide (something), to make (something) available for use.
To furnish or equip with.
The act of supplying.
An amount of something supplied.
Supplely: in a supple manner, with suppleness.

supply.ety:
From Middle English supplien, borrowed from Old French soupleer, souploier, from Latin suppleo (“to fill up, make full, complete, supply”).
The Middle English spelling was modified to conform to Latin etymology.

ex.en: The supply cannot keep up with the demand.
ex.ja: 供給が需要についていけない。

ex.en: Brazil supplies us with much of our coffee.
ex.ja: ブラジルはわが国のコーヒーの多くを供給している。

ex.en: Can you supply me with all I need?
ex.ja: あなたは私が必要としているものすべてを私に供給できますか。

note.ja: ラテン語 supplere ＝ sub（下から）+ plere（満たす）。「下から満たす」→「供給する」。complete と同じ ple。

en: Excess of material, useless by-products, or damaged, unsaleable products; garbage; rubbish.
Excrement or urine.
Barren; desert; empty.
Rejected as being defective; eliminated as being worthless; produced in excess.
To devastate; to destroy.
To squander (money or resources) uselessly; to spend (time) idly; to dissipate.

waste.ety: From Middle English wast, waste (“a waste”, noun), from Anglo-Norman, Old Northern French wast, waste (“a waste”), from Frankish *wōstī (“a waste”), from Proto-Germanic *wōstaz, *wōstuz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁weh₂- (“empty, wasted”). Displaced native Middle English wernen (“to refuse”) likely due to the similar sounding Middle English warnen

ex.en: It will end in a waste of labor.
ex.ja: それは骨折り損だ。

ex.en: It's a waste of time to stay longer.
ex.ja: これ以上待つのは時間の無駄だよ。

ex.en: The waste of time and money is incredible.
ex.ja: 時間とお金の浪費はとてつもない。

note.ja: ラテン語 vastus（空っぽの）から。「荒れた」→「無駄にする・廃棄物」。vast、devastate と同じ。

en: Having an unusually strange character or behaviour.
Deviating from the normal; bizarre.
A prediction.
That which comes to pass; a fact.
To destine; doom; change by witchcraft or sorcery.
To warn solemnly; adjure.

weird.ety:
From Middle English werde, wierde, wirde, wyrede, wurde, from Old English wyrd (“fate”), from Proto-West Germanic *wurdi, from Proto-Germanic *wurdiz, from Proto-Indo-European *wert- (“to turn, wind”). Cognate with Icelandic urður (“fate”). Related to Old English weorþan (“to become”); more at worth (verb).
Doublet of wyrd, a reborrowing of the original sense and spelling.
Obsolete by the 16th century in standard English. Its reintroduction is due to Shakespeare, who borrowed Middle Scots weird sisters, denoting the Fates of classical mythology, for the witches in his play Macbeth. Though orig

ex.en: I don't think that it's weird at all.
ex.ja: 全然変だと思わないんだけど。

ex.en: There was something weird about the incident.
ex.ja: その事件には何となく気味の悪いところがあった。

ex.en: You don't think that that is weird at all?
ex.ja: 君達、全然変だと思わないの？

note.ja: 古英語 wyrd（運命）から。シェイクスピア『マクベス』の魔女（weird sisters：運命の三姉妹）から「不気味な」→「変な」。

en: An animal that is full-grown.
A person who has reached the legal age of majority.
Fully grown.
Intended for or restricted to adults rather than children due to size, maturity, knowledge level, judgement, etc.

adult.ety: From French adulte, from Latin adultus (“grown up”), perfect passive participle of adolescō (“to grow up”). Compare adolescent.

ex.en: This is a book often read by adults.
ex.ja: この本は大人によく読まれている。

ex.en: This movie is for adults, not for children.
ex.ja: この映画は大人向けであり、子供向けではない。

ex.en: Most young adults enjoy going out at night.
ex.ja: 多くの若い成人は、晩に出かけることを好む。

note.ja: ラテン語 adultus（成長した）から。adolescere（成長する）の過去分詞。adolescent（青年）と同じ。

en: Seemingly; in appearance.
According to what the speaker has read or heard.

ex.ja: 一見したところ、この殺人は密室で起こっている。

ex.ja: どうやら２ヶ月以内に昇給がある感じだ。

ex.en: Apparently, Tom likes Mary quite a lot.
ex.ja: どうやら、トムはメアリーのことが大好きらしいよ。

note.ja: apparent（見かけの）+ -ly。「見たところ〜らしい」。appear と同じ。

en: A person who creates art.
A person who creates art as an occupation.

ex.en: The poor man finally became a great artist.
ex.ja: その貧しい男はついに偉大な芸術家になった。

ex.en: That artist created a lot of beautiful pictures.
ex.ja: その芸術家は数多くの美しい絵を創造した。

ex.en: John grew up to be a great artist.
ex.ja: ジョンは大きくなって偉大な芸術家になった。

note.ja: art（芸術）+ -ist。ラテン語 ars（技術）。「芸術家」。

en: A person presiding over a meeting, sometimes especially a man. (Compare chairwoman, chairperson, chair.)
The head of a corporate or governmental board of directors, a committee, or other formal entity.
To serve as chairman.

ex.ja: 私たちは彼をその会の議長に選んだ。

ex.en: Ten to one he will be elected chairman.
ex.ja: 十中八九、彼は議長に選ばれるであろう。

note.ja: chair（議長の席）+ man。「議長」。性別を問わない言い方は chairperson、chair。

en: A written work edited and published, as by a certain editor or in a certain manner, or at a certain time.
The whole number of copies of a work printed and published at one time.

edition.ety: From French édition, from Latin ēditiō, from ēdere (“to publish”).

ex.en: This edition is limited to seven thousand copies.
ex.ja: この版は7,000部に限定されています。

ex.en: The first edition was published ten years ago.
ex.ja: 初版は１０年前に出版された。

ex.en: This book still doesn't have a French edition.
ex.ja: この本のフランス語版はまだない。

note.ja: ラテン語 editio（出版）から。e（外へ）+ dare（与える）。「外に出すこと」→「版」。edit、editor と同じ。

en: A soldier engaged in designing or constructing military works for attack or defence, or other engineering works.
A person professionally engaged in the technical design and construction of large-scale private and public works such as bridges, buildin…
To employ one's abilities and knowledge as an engineer to design, construct, and/or maintain (something, such as a machine or a structure…
To use genetic engineering to alter or construct (a DNA sequence), or to alter (an organism).

ex.en: How many engineers took part in the conference?
ex.ja: 何人のエンジニアがその会議に参加しましたか。

ex.en: What made Bill decide to be an engineer?
ex.ja: どうしてビルはエンジニアになる決心をしたのか。

ex.en: Mr Smith had three sons who became engineers.
ex.ja: スミス氏には技師になった息子が３人いた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 engigneor（兵器を作る人）から。engine（からくり）。ラテン語 ingenium（才能）。ingenious と同じ。

en: A rating.
Performance on a test or other evaluation(s), expressed by a number, letter, or other symbol; a score.
To assign scores to the components of an academic test, or to overall academic performance.
To organize in grades.

grade.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French grade (“a grade, degree”), from Latin gradus (“a step, pace, degree”), from Proto-Italic *graðus, from Proto-Indo-European *gʰradʰ-, *gʰredʰ- (“to walk, go”). Doublet of gradus.
Cognate with Gothic 𐌲𐍂𐌹𐌸𐍃 (griþs, “step, grade”), Bavarian Gritt (“step, stride”), Lithuanian gri̇̀diju (“to go, wander”).

ex.en: What grade did you get on the test?
ex.ja: 試験の成績はどうだった。

ex.en: I want to buy two S-grade seats.
ex.ja: 特別席を二枚買いたい。

ex.en: I got a good grade in English.
ex.ja: 私は英語でよい成績を取った。

note.ja: ラテン語 gradus（段・歩み）から。grad（歩む）。一歩ずつの段階 →「等級・学年・成績」。gradual（段階的な）、graduate（段階を終える→卒業する）も同じ。

en: Enjoying good health; free from disease or disorder.
Conducive to health.

ex.ja: この男の子は、強くて健康な体を持っている。

ex.en: Walking is the best way to stay healthy.
ex.ja: 健康を維持するためには散歩するのが一番良い。

ex.en: Our school is surrounded by a healthy environment.
ex.ja: 私たちの学校は健全な環境に囲まれている。

note.ja: health（健康）+ -y。health は whole（完全な）、heal と同じ語根。

en: An organization founded to promote a cause
An institution of learning; a college, especially for technical subjects
To begin or initiate (something); to found.
To nominate; to appoint.

institute.ety: From French institut, from Middle French, from Latin īnstitūtum.

ex.en: The research institute was established in the late 1960s.
ex.ja: その研究所が設立されたのは１９６０年代後半です。

ex.en: He bestowed a large amount of money on the institute.
ex.ja: 彼は多額のお金を研究所に寄付した。

ex.en: We have established the institute with a view to facilitating the research.
ex.ja: われわれは研究を促進するために、この協会を設立した。

note.ja: in（中に）+ stit（立てる）+ ute。中に立てる →「設立する・研究所」。constitute（共に立てる→構成する）も同じ sta。

Systematicity, methodicalness, intentionality, order.
To apply a method to.
To apply particular treatment methods to (a mold).

ex.en: Our school has adopted a new teaching method.
ex.ja: 我が校は新しい教授法を採用した。

ex.en: The method was too expensive to be practical.
ex.ja: その方法は高くつきすぎて実用的でなかった。

ex.en: The company introduced Japanese methods into its business.
ex.ja: その会社は経営に日本式のやり方を導入した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 methodos（追究）から。meta（後を追って）+ hodos（道）。「道を追うこと」→「方法」。hod は episode と同じ。

On Monday.

From Middle English Monday, Monenday, from Old English mōnandæġ (“day of the moon”), from Proto-West Germanic *mānini dag, a calque (interpretātiō germānica) of Latin diēs Lūnae, equivalent to Moon + day. See also Japanese 月曜日 (“Moon's day”).

ex.ja: その博物館は月曜から金曜まで開いています。

ex.ja: その店は月曜から土曜まで開いている。

ex.ja: この仕事は月曜日までに終えねばならない。

en: In an obvious or clearly apparent manner.
Used as a filler word, or to introduce information even when not obvious.

From obvious + -ly.

ex.en: Tom is obviously very good with his hands.
ex.ja: トムは言うまでもなくとても手先が器用だ。

ex.en: Obviously, the server load will increase as a result.
ex.ja: 言うまでもなく、サーバの負荷が増大してしまうのです。

ex.en: He can speak French, and obviously English.
ex.ja: 彼はフランス語を話せる、ましてや英語は無論のことだ。

note.ja: obvious（明らかな）+ -ly。ラテン語 obvius（道で出会う）、ob + via（道）。「道で目の前にある」→「明らかな」。via と同じ。

en: One of a set of choices that can be made.
The freedom or right to choose.
To purchase an option on something.

option.ety: From French option, from Latin optiō (“choice; option; act of choosing”), from optō (“to choose, select”). Equivalent to opt + -ion.

ex.en: I would like to consider various options if necessary.
ex.ja: 必要とあれば色々と考えていきたい。

ex.en: What other options do I have?
ex.ja: 他にどんな選択肢があるの？

ex.en: I don't have any other option.
ex.ja: 他に選択肢はないんだよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 optio（選択）から。optare（選ぶ）。「選択肢」。adopt、opinion と同系。

en: A place or institution where people are held against their will, in the US especially for long-term confinement, as of those convicted of…
Confinement in prison (sense 1).
To imprison.

prison.ety: From Middle English prisoun, prison, from Old English prisūn, a borrowing from Old French prison, from Latin prehensiōnem, accusative singular of prehensiō, from the verb prehendō. Doublet of prehension.

ex.ja: 犯人は逮捕され、刑務所に入れられた。

ex.en: We can't put a young boy in prison.
ex.ja: 年のいかない少年を刑務所に入れることはできない。

ex.en: Tom was released from prison three months ago.
ex.ja: トムは３か月前に出所した。

note.ja: ラテン語 prehensio（捕らえること）から古フランス語を経た語。prehendere（つかむ）。prisoner、comprehend と同じ。

en: In some bicameral legislative systems, the upper house or chamber.
A group of experienced, respected, wise individuals serving as decision makers or advisors in a political system or in institutional gove…

senate.ety: From Middle English senat, from Old French senat, from Latin senātus (“council of elders; a senate”), from senex (“old”).

ex.en: He was elected to the Senate in the last election.
ex.ja: 彼は前回の選挙で上院議員に当選した。

note.ja: ラテン語 senatus（長老の会議）から。senex（年老いた）。→「上院・元老院」。senior（年上の）と同じ sen。

en: Some unspecified person.
Synonym of someone; an important person.
Any person.
A recognised or important person, a celebrity.

somebody.ety: From Middle English sum body, equivalent to some + body.

ex.en: There's somebody here who did it, isn't there?
ex.ja: だれか身に覚えのある人がいるんじゃないか。

ex.en: Somebody is standing in front of his room.
ex.ja: 誰かが彼の部屋の前にたっている。

ex.en: I hear he is somebody in his village.
ex.ja: 聞けば彼は村ではひとかどの人物だとか。

note.ja: some（ある）+ body（人）。「誰か」→「ひとかどの人物」。nobody の対。

A piece of such material: a block of stone, rock or a pebble.
Constructed of stone.

ex.en: Don't beat your head against a stone wall.
ex.ja: そんな無茶はよせ。

ex.en: That child threw a stone at the dog.
ex.ja: その子は犬に石を投げた。

ex.en: The house had a stone wall around it.
ex.ja: その家の周りに石垣があった。

note.ja: 古英語 stān から。「石」→ 重さの単位（14ポンド）。

en: The quality or degree of being strong.
The intensity of a force or power; potency.

strength.ety: From Middle English strengthe, from Old English strengþu (“strength”), from Proto-West Germanic *strangiþu (“strongness; strength”), equivalent to strong + -th (abstract nominal suffix). ex.en: I don't have the strength to keep trying.
ex.ja: 私にはやり続けるだけの強さがない。

ex.en: I have no strength to lift this stone.
ex.ja: 私にはこの石を持ち上げる力がない。

ex.en: He has the strength to survive the illness.
ex.ja: 彼にはその病気を乗り切るだけの力がある。

note.ja: strong（強い）+ -th。「強さ」。length（long）、width（wide）と同じ作り。

en: One who uses or makes use of something, a consumer or client or an express or implied licensee (free user) or a trespasser.
A person who uses drugs, especially illegal drugs.

user.ety: From Middle English usere, equivalent to use + -er. Cognate with Scots usar, uiser (“user”).

ex.en: Are you sure you want to block this user?
ex.ja: 本当にこのユーザーをブロックしますか？

ex.en: Refer to the Users' Guide if you have any problems.
ex.ja: もし困った事があればユーザーズガイドにあたってください。

ex.en: Would you like to become a trusted user?
ex.ja: 「信頼できるユーザー」になりたいですか？

note.ja: use（使う）+ -er。ラテン語 uti（使う）。「利用者」。

en: Especially, being of the wild type: being of an unbroken ancestral line of undomesticated animals, as opposed to being feral, being an un…
Being in the wild, by any pathway (whether by being of the wild type, by being feral since birth, or by being feral after escape from dom…
Inaccurately; not on target.
Intended to be synchronized with film or video but recorded separately.
The undomesticated state of a wild animal.
A wilderness.

wild.ety:

From Middle English casten, from Old Norse kasta (“to throw, cast, overturn”), from Proto-Germanic *kastōną (“to throw, cast”), of unknown origin.
Cognate with Scots cast (“to cast, throw”), Danish kaste (“to throw”), Swedish kasta (“to throw, cast, fling, toss, discard”), Icelandic kasta (“to pitch, toss”). In the sense of "flinging", displaced native warp.
The senses relating to broadcasting are based on that same term; compare -cast.

ex.ja: その研究は問題に新たな光を投げかけた。

ex.en: I cast my fishing line into the sea.
ex.ja: 私は釣り糸を海に投げ入れた。
